AIML Module Project - Featurization, Model Selection and Tuning - Aaditya Kumar Ravi¶

*DOMAIN:* Semiconductor manufacturing process
*CONTEXT:* A complex modern semiconductor manufacturing process is normally under constant surveillance via the monitoring of signals/variables collected from sensors and or process measurement points. However, not all of these signals are equally valuable in a specific monitoring system. The measured signals contain a combination of useful information, irrelevant information as well as noise. Engineers typically have a much larger number of signals than are actually required. If we consider each type of signal as a feature, then feature selection may be applied to identify the most relevant signals. The Process Engineers may then use these signals to determine key factors contributing to yield excursions downstream in the process. This will enable an increase in process throughput, decreased time to learning and reduce the per unit production costs. These signals can be used as features to predict the yield type. And by analysing and trying out different combinations of features, essential signals that are impacting the yield type can be identified.
*DATA DESCRIPTION:* signal-data.csv : (1567, 592)
The data consists of 1567 datapoints each with 591 features.
The dataset presented in this case represents a selection of such features where each example represents a single production entity with associated measured features and the labels represent a simple pass/fail yield for in house line testing. Target column “ –1” corresponds to a pass and “1” corresponds to a fail and the data time stamp is for that specific test point.
*PROJECT OBJECTIVE:* We will build a classifier to predict the Pass/Fail yield of a particular process entity and analyse whether all the features are required to build the model or not.
*Steps and tasks: [Total Score: 60 points]*
*1. Import and understand the data. [5 Marks]*

Observations:

  • The minimum, Q1, median, and Q3 values are all the same -1 for Pass/Fail feature which indicates that at least 75% of the data falls at this value. It means that the dataset feature Pass/Fail is heavily skewed towards one value -1 i.e imbalanced.
  • Column 5 has all min, 25%, 50%, 75%, max values same i.e 100, which indicates it has only one value i.e 100. This can be removed as it does not provide any discriminatory or useful information for modeling or analysis.

2. Data cleansing: [15 Marks]¶
A. Write a for loop which will remove all the features with 20%+ Null values and impute rest with mean of the feature. [5 Marks]¶
In [317]:
signal_df.shape
Out[317]:
(1567, 592)
  • We have 3 types of values in the dataset object, int, float. so it is not possible to find mean of object type. hence we will exclude object datatype while finding mean and replacing with mean of the column.
  • We have total 592 features before removal.
In [318]:
for col in signal_df.columns:
    missing_perc = signal_df[col].isnull().mean()*100
    if missing_perc > 20:  #20%+ missing values check
        signal_df.drop(col, axis=1, inplace=True)
    else:
        if signal_df[col].dtype!='O':  #excluding object type
            col_mean = signal_df[col].mean()
            signal_df[col].fillna(col_mean, inplace=True)
In [319]:
#After removing columns with 20%+ null values and imputing rest with mean, Let us view the percentage count

  • We can see all the columns having 20%+ missing values are removed. and rest are replaced with its column mean
  • Now we have only 560 columns left out of 592 as 32 columns got removed due to having 20%+ missing values

B. Identify and drop the features which are having same value for all the rows. [3 Marks]¶

In [322]:
signal_df.duplicated().sum()
Out[322]:
0

There is no duplicate rows found, Let us check after removing 1st column from the search as Time can not be same.

In [323]:
signal_df.iloc[:,1:].duplicated().sum()
Out[323]:
0
  • Still we don't find any duplicate value, it looks like there is no more than 1 row with same values for entire columns, meaning there is no duplicate rows for all features together.
  • Now let us identify those features individually which are having same values for all the rows.
In [324]:
for col in signal_df.columns:
    #Get how many unique values are there for particular column, if the column has only one value for all rows it means the column has duplicated value for that column.
    #we will drop those columns
    col_value_count = signal_df[col].nunique() 
    if col_value_count==1:
        signal_df.drop(col, axis=1, inplace=True)

C. Drop other features if required using relevant functional knowledge. Clearly justify the same. [2 Marks]¶

And¶

D. Check for multi-collinearity in the data and take necessary action. [3 Marks]¶

  • Still we have 444 columns present in the dataset which is quite high. Having a large number of features can lead to several challenges including increased computational complexity, difficulty in visualization, overfitting, and decreased interpretability. Hence, we should try to reduce the number of features to improve model performance and efficiency.
  • Let us drop those columns whose standard deviation is 0 as columns with 0 standard deviation remains constant for all and is not much useful for model building.
In [327]:
std_dev = signal_df.iloc[:,1:].std() #excluded 1st feature as that is of object type 
cols_with_zero_std = std_dev[std_dev==0].index
cols_with_zero_std
Out[327]:
Index([], dtype='object')

there are no columns with standard deviation zero, otherwise we would have dropped them as it does not give any useful information for model building.

  • Let us check if there is high correlation between any columns. we may drop those columns which has high correlation with more than equal 8 other columns.
  • Commonly used threshold for considering correlations as high is 0.7 to 0.9 for positive and -0.7 to -0.9 for negative. we are not taking 1 correlation value here as we are excluding self correlation. diagonal(self) correlation are always 1.

high_corr_indices = []

#Iterate over the elements of the correlation matrix up to the diagonal only, becuase beyond diagonal elements are repeated.
for i in range(len(corr_matrix)):
    for j in range(i):
        if abs(corr_matrix.iloc[i, j]) > 0.7: #assuming 0.7 or above is higher correlation (+ve and -ve)
            high_corr_indices.append((corr_matrix.index[i], corr_matrix.columns[j]))

print(high_corr_indices) #print indices having high correlation

count_dict = {}
for pair in high_corr_indices:
    x_value = pair[0]  #Get the first element x of the pair
    count_dict[x_value] = count_dict.get(x_value, 0) + 1  #Increment the count for the x value

for x_value, count in count_dict.items():
    print(x_value, "occurs", count, "times")
    if count>=8: #Here we are assuming 8 columns as threshold for correlation with other columns as we have most of the columns are correlated for less than 8 times, 
                 #a few are having more than 8 correlations and I checked they are representing almost similar information. 
                 #Hence considering that we need to reduce the correlations, dimension reduction and redundant data, Choosing 8 here.  
        signal_df.drop(x_value, axis=1, inplace=True) #dropping columns having high correlation with more than equal to 8 columns

print(signal_df.shape)

  • Let us try Lasso regularization method because Lasso regression is particularly useful when dealing with high-dimensional datasets with many irrelevant or redundant features. It can automatically perform feature selection and create simpler, more interpretable models.
  • it can indirectly address multicollinearity by forcing some coefficients to be exactly zero, effectively selecting a subset of features and reducing the effective dimensionality of the problem.

from sklearn.linear_model import Lasso, Ridge
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn import preprocessing

X=signal_df.drop(['Time','Pass/Fail'], axis=1)
Y=signal_df['Pass/Fail']

X_scaled = preprocessing.scale(X)
Y_scaled = preprocessing.scale(Y)

X_train, X_test, Y_train, Y_test = train_test_split(X_scaled, Y_scaled, test_size=0.25, random_state=1)

#We will try different values of alpha and will pick one with best training and test score among that. 
alphas = np.logspace(-4, 2, 100) 
for a in alphas:
    lasso = Lasso(alpha=a)
    lasso.fit(X_train,Y_train)
    coeff = lasso.coef_
    print("=========Alpha:",a,"===============")
    print("Lasso Train Score:",lasso.score(X_train, Y_train))
    print("Lasso Test Score",lasso.score(X_test, Y_test))
    print("Lasso coefficients(Not Zero):",coeff[coeff!=0])

E. Make all relevant modifications on the data using both functional/logical reasoning/assumptions. [2 Marks]¶

We have done so many modifications on data already, Here is the list of modifications done with assumptions and reasoning as below:

  • Initially we had 1592 rows and 592 columns which was very high number of columns, which we have reduced it to 1567 rows and 66 columns so far. Having high number of columns is a curse of dimensionality and it causes increased computational complexity, overfitting, difficulty in visualizations etc.
  • We did missing value treatment. Those columns having more than 20% missing values, we have dropped those columns, and columns having less than 20% missing values, we have replaced it with mean of that column values. Since Missing values could potentially impact the model's performance, we have done the steps to mitigate that.
  • We have also dropped those features which have only one constant value for all the rows. Columns with constant values offer no variability in the data. As a result, they do not provide any useful information to the model during training, so we dropped those.
  • Also, dropped columns having standard deviation 0 as such columns causes no variability, redundancy and overfitting and is not much useful for good model building.
  • We also checked for no duplicated rows as duplicated rows gives redundant information.
  • We also checked for high correlation and dropped few columns with high correlations.
  • Then we applied Lasso regularization method because Lasso regression is particularly useful when dealing with high-dimensional datasets with many irrelevant or redundant features. It can automatically perform feature selection and create simpler, more interpretable models. it can indirectly address multicollinearity by forcing some coefficients to be exactly zero, effectively selecting a subset of features and reducing the effective dimensionality of the problem.
  • We also did scaling on dataset while doing Lasso regularization as scaling standardize the features, enahnce model perofrmance as it ensures all the features are on the same scale.

Further Scope of improvement on data:

  • We can further do PCA for dimensionality reduction as we still have total 66 columns in the dataset.
  • We can also do target variabe balancing as target variable is imbalanced with 93:7% ratio.
  • We can also do outlier treatment.

4. Data pre-processing: [10 Marks]¶

A. Segregate predictors vs target attributes. [2 Marks]¶

In [441]:
#Segregating all variables except Pass/Fail as predictors
X = signal_df_copy.drop('Pass/Fail', axis=1)
#Segregating Pass/Fail variable as target variable
Y = signal_df_copy['Pass/Fail']

B. Check for target balancing and fix it if found imbalanced. [3 Marks]¶

We see that 1463 (93.3%) values represent Pass class whereas, 104 (6.6%) values represents Fail class which is highly imbalanced.
We will do upsampling for minority class i.e 1 Fail using SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over Sampling Technique) from imblearn library.
Since, SMOTE should only be applied to the training data only, not to the entire dataset (including both training and testing data) to avoid data leakage, realistic evaluation and maintain class distribution on test. So, We will first do the train test split, SMOTE and then standardization.

In [444]:
#train test split
X_train, X_test, Y_train, Y_test = train_test_split(X, Y, test_size=0.25, stratify=Y, random_state=1)

5. Model training, testing and tuning: [20 Marks] ]¶

In [519]:
from sklearn import metrics
In [565]:
#defining this variable to record the performance of each model. This is for further model perofrmance summary comparision
performance_summary_all = pd.DataFrame(columns=[
    'Method', 'train_accuracy', 'train_recall', 'train_precision', 'train_f1',
    'test_accuracy', 'test_recall', 'test_precision', 'test_f1'
])
In [566]:
''' 
    Defining a generic method to train, predict and print different performance metrics(Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score), 
    classification report and confustion matrix. We will use this method throughout this project.
'''
def train_predict_perfscore_confmatrix(model, method):
    '''
    train, Predict, Print performance scores and confusion matrix for a classifier model.

    Parameters:
    - model: Classifier model
    - method: model name for testing.
    '''
    global performance_summary_all
    
    model.fit(X_train, Y_train) #train the model
    
    pred_train = model.predict(X_train) #predit on training data
    pred_test = model.predict(X_test)   #predit on testing data
    
    train_accuracy = model.score(X_train, Y_train) #score on training data
    test_accuracy = model.score(X_test, Y_test)    #score on testing data
    
    train_recall = metrics.recall_score(Y_train, pred_train) #recall on training data
    test_recall = metrics.recall_score(Y_test, pred_test)    #recall on testing data
    
    train_precision = metrics.precision_score(Y_train, pred_train) #precision on training data
    test_precision = metrics.precision_score(Y_test, pred_test)    #precision on testing data
    
    train_f1 = metrics.f1_score(Y_train, pred_train) #f1 score on training data
    test_f1 = metrics.f1_score(Y_test, pred_test)    #f1 score on testing data
    
    new_result = pd.DataFrame({
        'Method': [method],
        'train_accuracy': [train_accuracy],
        'train_recall': [train_recall],
        'train_precision': [train_precision],
        'train_f1': [train_f1],
        'test_accuracy': [test_accuracy],
        'test_recall': [test_recall],
        'test_precision': [test_precision],
        'test_f1': [test_f1]
    })
    # Concatenate new_result dataframe to existing global performance_summary_all which is used to record perforamnces of 
    # each run. This variable will be used further whenever we want to do the comparision on performances of each run.
    performance_summary_all = pd.concat([performance_summary_all, new_result], ignore_index=True)
    # It should not duplicate values of same method when we re-run. it should keep the latest one and drop all previous ones.
    performance_summary_all.drop_duplicates(subset='Method', keep='last')
    
    print("================Performance Score================")
    print("Accuracy on training dataset : ", train_accuracy)
    print("Accuracy on test dataset : ", test_accuracy)
    
    print("\nRecall on training dataset : ", train_recall)
    print("Recall on test dataset : ", test_recall)
    
    print("\nPrecision on training dataset : ", train_precision)
    print("Precision on test dataset : ", test_precision)
    
    print("\nF1-Score on training dataset : ", train_f1)
    print("F1-Score on test dataset : ", test_f1)
    
    print("\n================Classfication Report for test data=============")
    print(metrics.classification_report(Y_test, pred_test)) 
    
    print("\n================Confusion Matrix for test data=================")
    cm = metrics.confusion_matrix(Y_test, pred_test, labels=[-1, 1])
    df_cm = pd.DataFrame(cm, index=['-1', ' 1'], columns=['Pred -1', 'Pred 1'])
    print(df_cm)

A. Use any Supervised Learning technique to train a model. [2 Marks]¶

We will use KNeighborsClassifier supervised learning technique to train the model on the balanced and standardized train data.

In [567]:

''' 
    Defining a generic method to PCA train, predict and print different performance metrics(Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score), 
    classification report and confustion matrix. We will use this method throughout this project.
'''
def PCAtrain_predict_perfscore_confmatrix(model, method):
    '''
    train, Predict, Print performance scores and confusion matrix for a classifier model.

    Parameters:
    - model: Classifier model
    - method: model name for testing.
    '''
    global performance_summary_all
    
    model.fit(X_train_pca48, Y_train) #train the model
    
    pred_train = model.predict(X_train_pca48) #predit on training data
    pred_test = model.predict(X_test_pca48)   #predit on testing data
    
    train_accuracy = model.score(X_train_pca48, Y_train) #score on training data
    test_accuracy = model.score(X_test_pca48, Y_test)    #score on testing data
    
    train_recall = metrics.recall_score(Y_train, pred_train) #recall on training data
    test_recall = metrics.recall_score(Y_test, pred_test)    #recall on testing data
    
    train_precision = metrics.precision_score(Y_train, pred_train) #precision on training data
    test_precision = metrics.precision_score(Y_test, pred_test)    #precision on testing data
    
    train_f1 = metrics.f1_score(Y_train, pred_train) #f1 score on training data
    test_f1 = metrics.f1_score(Y_test, pred_test)    #f1 score on testing data
    
    new_result = pd.DataFrame({
        'Method': [method],
        'train_accuracy': [train_accuracy],
        'train_recall': [train_recall],
        'train_precision': [train_precision],
        'train_f1': [train_f1],
        'test_accuracy': [test_accuracy],
        'test_recall': [test_recall],
        'test_precision': [test_precision],
        'test_f1': [test_f1]
    })
    # Concatenate new_result dataframe to existing global performance_summary_all which is used to record perforamnces of 
    # each run. This variable will be used further whenever we want to do the comparision on performances of each run.
    performance_summary_all = pd.concat([performance_summary_all, new_result], ignore_index=True)
    # It should not duplicate values of same method when we re-run. it should keep the latest one and drop all previous ones.
    performance_summary_all.drop_duplicates(subset='Method', keep='last')
    
    print("================Performance Score================")
    print("Accuracy on training dataset : ", train_accuracy)
    print("Accuracy on test dataset : ", test_accuracy)
    
    print("\nRecall on training dataset : ", train_recall)
    print("Recall on test dataset : ", test_recall)
    
    print("\nPrecision on training dataset : ", train_precision)
    print("Precision on test dataset : ", test_precision)
    
    print("\nF1-Score on training dataset : ", train_f1)
    print("F1-Score on test dataset : ", test_f1)
    
    print("\n================Classfication Report for test data=============")
    print(metrics.classification_report(Y_test, pred_test)) 
    
    print("\n================Confusion Matrix for test data=================")
    cm = metrics.confusion_matrix(Y_test, pred_test, labels=[-1, 1])
    df_cm = pd.DataFrame(cm, index=['-1', ' 1'], columns=['Pred -1', 'Pred 1'])
    print(df_cm)

Insights Classification Report:

  • Accuracy on training data is high 89.8% which indicates model performs well on training data but accuracy on test data is relatively lower 54.5%. It is indicating towards model is overfit to training data.
  • Recall on training is perfect 1.0 which indicates that the model correctly identifies all instances of the -1(pass). and on test data also, recall is relatively good which says on test data as well it can identify significant instances of -1 (pass).
  • Precision on training data is moderate 83%, but on test data is extremely low 10%, which indicates that a large portion of the instances predicted as fail are actually pass.
  • F1-score, which balances precision and recall, is high on the training dataset 90% but significantly lower on the test dataset 18% which says that the model's overall performance decreases on unseen data.
  • Detailed classification report for each class i.e -1 Pass and 1 Fail, Model performs relatively well in predicting -1 pass compared to 1 fail
  • Precision, recall, f1-score for -1 Pass class is 97%, 53%, 69% but for 1 Fail is 10%, 77%, 18% respectively which is comparitively less.
  • Overall accuracy we got on test data is just 55%, is indicating towards overfit.
  • If we look at confustion matrix, it indicates that large portion 194 of Pass (True Positive) is correctly predicted as pass.
    but large portion 172 (False Negative) was predicted as fail 1 but was actually pass -1. 20 is correctly predicted as fail was actually fail i.e 1 (True Negative), but 6 who were actually fail but predicted as pass -1(False Positive).

B. Select the final best trained model along with your detailed comments for selecting this model. [1 Marks]¶

Looking at all the above comparision of all the models tried out so far, the best model seems to be:

  • SVM-GridSearchCV score for train_accuracy, train_recall, train_precision, train_f1, test_accuracy, test_recall, test_precision, test_f1 are 1.000000, 1.000000, 1.000000, 1.000000, 0.895408, 0.269231, 0.241379, 0.254545 respectively.
  • Train Accuracy, Recall, Precision, F1 All have perfect scores of 1. This indicates that the model is performing extremely well on the training data, correctly predicting all instances of both classes -1(pass), 1(fail) with high precision and recall.
  • Test accuracy is 0.895408, which is relatively high. It indicates that the model is performing well on unseen data and correctly classifying approximately 89.5% of the instances, which no other model is prediciting so well on test data.
  • Test recall is 0.269231 which suggests that the model is able to correctly identify around 26.92% of the failed cases i.e 1 out of all actual failed cases in the test set.
  • Test precision is 0.241379, which is relatively low. It means that out of all instances predicted as failed i.e 1 by the model, only approximately 24.14% are actually true failures.
  • Below is the classification report and confusion matrix for this model.

  • It made mistake while predicting with 22 and 19 data points. 22 was identified as fail but they were actually pass.
  • 19 was actually fail but model predicted it as pass.
  • but the number of mistakes in prediction is very less than number of correct predictions. Hence I think it is the best model.
  • If we look at the classification report as well, prediction for pass is quite good around 95% with similar recall and precision for pass. but yes for fail it is quite low but comparatively better than other models trained.

D. Write your conclusion on the results. [1 Marks]¶

The conclusions drawn from this project case study results can be summarized as follows:

  • Overall, we could find a good model from accuracy perspective but still precision, recall and f1-score has scope of improvement.
  • We can try different grid search with different prameters for hyper parameter tuning and training the model with best model found out of grid search.
  • We could see feature importances and based on that we could select the features.
  • We can be more careful while dropping the features, may be using forward selection or backward elimination based on the performance score with particular feature and without particular feature. but that will be very time taking process to try using different set of models and model perforamnce depends on different combination of features as well.
  • The selected model achieved high accuracy and recall on the training dataset, indicating excellent performance in predicting both pass and fail outcomes. However, on the test dataset, the model's performance degraded slightly which suggests some overfitting on the training data.
  • Finally, the selected model was pickled for future use ensuring that the trained model can be easily loaded and deployed in production environments without the need for retraining.
